The change is complete and correct. 

The `AnyJsImportLike` query type (shared by this rule) already matches all three import forms — `JsModuleSource` (ES static imports), `JsCallExpression` (CommonJS `require()`), and `JsImportCallExpression` (dynamic `import()`) — and `is_node_builtin_module` recognizes both bare names (`fs`, `path`) and `node:`-prefixed names (the list contains both variants). Since the diagnostic message lives in a single `diagnostic()` method, the corrected wording applies uniformly to every detected violation.

- Before: `"Using Node.js modules are forbidden."`
- After: `"Using Node.js modules is forbidden."`
